title: Design and construction of a low-cost nose poke system for rodents
author: Rizzi, Lodge, et al.

steps.title: Gather electronic components
steps.instruction: Collect all parts listed in Table 1, including an Arduino UNO board, red LEDs (LED1), green LEDs (LED2), light‑dependent resistors (LDRs), a 100 Ω resistor (R1), a 120 Ω resistor (R2), a 10 kΩ resistor (R3), a BNC connector (GMP S.A. MBL‑F‑473‑500 mW), a breadboard, jumper wires, and a 3‑D‑printed Arduino case.

steps.title: Assemble red LED‑LDR circuits
steps.instruction: For each of the four ports, connect a red LED in series with a 100 Ω resistor (R1) to the Arduino 5 V pin and ground; connect each LDR between the Arduino 3.3 V pin and analog‑in ports A1‑A4, and place a 10 kΩ resistor (R3) from the LDR to ground to form a voltage divider.

steps.title: Assemble green LED circuits
steps.instruction: Connect each green LED (LED2) to digital ports D8, D9, D10, and D11 through a 120 Ω resistor (R2), then connect the LED cathodes to ground; these LEDs will illuminate when the red‑LED/LDR beam is interrupted.

steps.title: Connect BNC output
steps.instruction: Wire digital port D13 to the live contact of the BNC connector and connect the BNC shielding to Arduino ground; this output will drive the laser for optogenetic stimulation.

steps.title: Build PVC frame
steps.instruction: Construct a rectangular PVC box (open‑field style) with two semi‑closed compartments: a front mouse compartment and a rear electronics compartment. In the front wall cut four 15 mm diameter nose‑poke holes equally spaced, each with its lower edge 1 cm above the floor and a 5 mm diameter hole directly above to hold a green LED. In the rear compartment, position 5 mm holes directly above and below each nose port to hold a red LED above and an LDR below, aligning them vertically.

steps.title: Mount electronics on frame
steps.instruction: Place the breadboard with all resistors inside the rear compartment, secure the Arduino UNO in the 3‑D‑printed case, and attach the case to the frame. Insert the red LEDs, green LEDs, and LDRs into their respective holes so that the red LED shines onto the LDR and the green LED sits above each port.

steps.title: Load Arduino sketch
steps.instruction: Connect the Arduino UNO to a computer via USB (or external power adapter), open the Arduino IDE, load the supplied sketch (Supplementary File 2), and upload it to the board.

steps.title: Set up serial communication
steps.instruction: In the Arduino IDE open the Serial Monitor; the board will reset and transmit a header line listing port number, poke number, and timestamp. Each nose poke will then be sent as a comma‑separated row. At the end of a session manually copy the text to a file and save it as a CSV. Closing and reopening the Serial Monitor resets the board for the next session.

steps.title: Optional automated data capture
steps.instruction: Use third‑party serial‑monitor software or a secondary script to automatically record and store the CSV data instead of manual copying.

steps.title: Prepare transgenic mice
steps.instruction: Obtain DAT‑CRE mice (Jackson Laboratory stock 006660), 6–8 weeks old (n = 3). Perform stereotactic surgery: inject 300 nl of AAV5‑EF1α‑DIO‑ChR2‑H134R‑EYFP bilaterally at coordinates –3.4 mm AP, 0.45 mm ML, 4.35 mm DV from bregma, and implant a single optic fiber at a 10° angle above the VTA.

steps.title: Configure Arduino for testing
steps.instruction: Modify the uploaded sketch to deactivate the two central ports, leaving only the lateral ports active. Program the BNC output to trigger a 3 s laser pulse at 50 Hz with 5 ms pulse width when the active port is poked; during the 3 s light delivery the system should ignore further nose‑poke inputs.

steps.title: Run daily nose‑poke sessions
steps.instruction: Three weeks after surgery, place each mouse in the nose‑poke system for a 60 min session, repeat for six consecutive days. Record behavior with AnyMaze software, which automatically quantifies time spent near active and inactive ports. Simultaneously monitor nose‑poke events via the Arduino serial monitor and log them as CSV.

steps.title: Post‑experiment tissue verification
steps.instruction: After the sixth session, perfuse animals intracardially, fix brains, slice, and verify ChR2 expression and optic‑fiber placement in the VTA by confocal imaging and TH immunostaining.
